## Design

### 2026-10-07 – I downloaded KiCad, used a template for a Pi HAT and an Esp32 S3 and worked a ton on it and mostly labeled things. I worked a ton on the boot and reset circuits with power buttons and stuff. It was re

**1h**

I downloaded KiCad, used a template for a Pi HAT and an Esp32 S3 and worked a ton on it and mostly labeled things. I worked a ton on the boot and reset circuits with power buttons and stuff. It was really cool. I think I'm doing good and soon enough I will be done, slowly but surely. I also labeled the TX and RX for connecting the ESP32 S3 to the Pi.

### 2026-10-07 – I basically made the 16 GPIO ports, the 2 servo connectors for my arm, and added a chip for the usb ports. It looks massive but I'm sure I will be done soon. It's completely possible. The wiring took

**2h**

I basically made the 16 GPIO ports, the 2 servo connectors for my arm, and added a chip for the usb ports. It looks massive but I'm sure I will be done soon. It's completely possible. The wiring took forever though. Writing the name of the labels takes so long! Thank goodness KiCad has a feature where you just have to write the name and it automatically connects it. Routing it will take FOREVER though.

### 2026-10-08 – Lots of changes happened, I realized that it's the schematic not the pcb, I learned and tested lots of things, I changed the power distribution to go through different traces for safety, I added a fus

**2.5h**

Lots of changes happened, I realized that it's the schematic not the pcb, I learned and tested lots of things, I changed the power distribution to go through different traces for safety, I added a fuse and some capacitors for safety, and I am almost done with the PCB.

### 2026-10-08 – I ran a lot of checks and KiCad's built in electronics checker and I found out all the errors as at first I had 30 errors and now there's none after hunting down all of the errors, I assigned footprin

**2.5h**

I ran a lot of checks and KiCad's built in electronics checker and I found out all the errors as at first I had 30 errors and now there's none after hunting down all of the errors, I assigned footprints to all of the parts, I fixed the previous USB errors and the voltage regulators, I fixed the buttons, and the PI connectors. I'm planning on having a mini-pcb too for the 2 servos at the very front of my arm. I'll try to make that first in order to learn how to route and design these things! It's extremely fun! Thank you so much for this!
